Subject: Re: Quick recap + clarifying ask from today's demo

Evan — great questions, thank you. Quick answers up front and a proposed next step (pilot SOW + benchmarks).

Short answers:
- Truncation: the demo used a hybrid approach — long-sequence model (32k+ KV cache) for the most recent window, plus a prefix-summarization step for the oldest sections. We avoid blind tail-chopping by creating overlapping summaries for preceding chunks and feeding them as condensed context. That mitigates coverage loss for leading context.
- Benchmarks: attached is a quick CSV with our internal run on 50 anonymized notes (careledger_longdoc_benchmarks.csv). Columns: model, context_config, avg_latency_ms, ROUGE-L, BERTScore, faithfulness-rate (human label).

Recommended shortlist for pilots (balanced cost vs fidelity):
- Redwood-Max-32k-v2 (best fidelity on 20–40k docs; slower but higher faithfulness)
- Redwood-Lite-70B-8k with progressive retrieval (cheaper, acceptable when you can RAG older sections)
- Mistral-2-22B-32k (good latency/cost midpoint for 30k notes)

Suggested evaluation checklist for your team (short prompt set attached: prompt_set_v1.txt):
- Fidelity: 10 targeted QA checks per note (does the summary preserve primary diagnosis, meds, discharge instructions?)
- Completeness: percent of key-section coverage (admission hx, procedures, meds)
- Hallucination rate: labeled by clinician review on a stratified sample

Pilot SOW proposal (high level):
- 2-week ingest + run-on 200 de-identified notes
- Compare 3 model/configs above with the same prompt set
- Deliverable: CSV benchmark + 20 clinician annotations + recommendations
- Estimated Redwood-hosted cost: $5–8k for the run (depending on tokenization and reruns).

Next steps:
1) If this looks good, I'll send a short SOW draft (attached: pilot-sow-draft.pdf).
2) We can provision a sandbox workspace and provide a one-click runbook so your team can reproduce results.

Notes on risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Summaries compressing leading context too aggressively. Mitigation: overlapping chunk summaries + anchor prompts that force mention of lead sections.
- Risk: Regression from quantization on hallucination. Mitigation: baseline on float32 / q8_0 and q4 runs; prefer q8_0 for fidelity-critical runs.

I'll follow up internally with Neha and Marissa on the detailed prompt designs and the eval rubric.

Cheers,
Priyom Das
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
(attachment: careledger_longdoc_benchmarks.csv, prompt_set_v1.txt, pilot-sow-draft.pdf)

Couple internal notes for the pilot deliverable so we present defensible comparisons: 
- Make sure we include a "truncation stress test" case: artificially prepend an important 2–3 sentence objective at the top of notes to see whether chunking + overlap reliably preserves it. Include recall@section for that objective.
- Add a condition for "progressive summarization" vs "flat chunk+concat". Progressive (summarize chunk -> summarize summary+next chunk) usually reduces token use and can surface lead context better.
- Add an explicit check for prompt injection artifacts when older summaries are included verbatim.

I can own the eval rubric and labeler instructions. Priyom — can you give me the raw run outputs (JSONL) from the benchmark so I can instrument the scoring script? If not, provide a CSV with fields: note_id, model, config, prompt_hash, summary_text, latency_ms.

Neha
